attrs.evidence: (⟸) a split cycle is 2-connected, hence contained in one block, which then carries ≥2 sites. (⟹) any two edges of a block lie on a common cycle, so a block with two sites yields a split cycle. Checked against brute-force enumeration of every simple cycle (including 2-cycles from parallel edges) on 117,648 federations: 0 mismatches.
attrs.prior_art: Block decomposition: Whitney 1932; Diestel Graph Theory §3.1.
attrs.statement: κₛ(G, site) := Σ over blocks B of max(0, |sites(B)| − 1) is zero exactly when no cycle of the carrier is split across sites.
